answer: In an agent-run saffron market at a jetty, each seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before its offers enter buyers' search results. Creating hollow identities is easy, but activating 1,000 of them requires $100,000 tied up for a month. Closing an account does not release its bond early, so an attacker cannot recycle the same funds rapidly across aliases; scaling the attack demands proportionally more capital.
